facility_desc: Amazon fulfillment center, 9201 S Portland Ave (640,000 sf, Will Rogers World Airport area; leased on airport trust land)
program: OKC Strategic Investment Program job-creation incentive (OKC Economic Development Trust, GOLT bond fund) plus road improvements
issuer: Oklahoma City Economic Development Trust (audited financial statements FY2018-FY2021); City Council
notes: Primary: the Trust's audited statements (June 30 2018, note GOLT Bond Funded Commitments, p.42) list Amazon.com with an outstanding award of 1,700,000 (nothing the year before); FY2019 and FY2020 also 1,700,000; FY2021 1,600,000 (the 100,000 fall is not explained in the note, so it is not recorded as realized). Components per AP via KJRH 2018-05-23: $1 million in public payments to Amazon for more than 50 managerial jobs plus $700,000 in city road improvements; do not add them to the 1.7M. Journal Record 2018-05-15: Trust approved 4-0 on 2018-05-15, money from GOLT bonds, released only if Amazon creates at least 53 new-to-market jobs within 5 years (avg wage about 60,000); Amazon promised 1,750 jobs overall. AP: City Council voted 5-2 on 2018-05-22 to authorize staff to negotiate the agreement; Journal Record 2019-02-26 reports Council approval of the joint economic development agreement (Feb 2019, building about 75 pct finished). Investment: 153M (Journal Record) vs 146M in OK Energy Today. Lease: 40 years at 242,039.26 a year (OK Energy Today, 2018-05-14), a lease, not a subsidy. Secondary: https://journalrecord.com/2018/05/15/okc-trust-approves-incentives-for-amazon-center/ ; https://apnews.com/general-news-7de280a5233d409fb2c8974af0be0983 ; https://freepressokc.com/amazon-incentive-deal-approved-okc-council-over-objections/ . Council agenda/resolution text itself not obtained (agenda.okc.gov behind Incapsula).

facility_desc: Amazon fulfillment center, 4040 N 125th East Ave (about 2.5M sf; opened Aug 2020): water and sewer lines on 125th East Ave and 43rd St N
program: Tulsa Metropolitan Utility Authority (TMUA) allocation for water and wastewater lines (public infrastructure, benefits future development too)
issuer: Tulsa Metropolitan Utility Authority (as reported by Tulsa World)
notes: Tulsa World 2018-06-20 'Amazon details/incentives' box: TMUA 'has agreed to allocate $1.3 million, which includes a contingency' for a water line along 125th East Ave and 43rd St N and a wastewater line along 43rd St N. Public infrastructure, not a payment to Amazon; the article says much of it is meant to benefit future development as well. Tulsa Mayor's office / TMUA agenda not obtained. Same package as the 940,000 traffic row below (the Journal Record 2019 'Tulsa committed $2.3 million' is about the sum of the two, 2.24M). Oklahoma Dept of Commerce told Tulsa World it could not say whether it gave incentives; Cherokee Nation cited an NDA; ODOT advanced traffic-signal work at 46th St N and US 169 (no amount); Tulsa Tech flexible training incentive (no amount). Amazon press release 2018-06-08 gives no amount.

facility_desc: Amazon fulfillment center, 4040 N 125th East Ave: traffic signals and turn lanes (36th St N and Garnett Rd; 46th St N and 125th East Ave; 36th St N and 125th East Ave)
program: City of Tulsa Economic Development Infrastructure Fund (public road work)

facility_desc: Amazon sortation center, 270,000 sf, SE corner of N Mingo Rd and 36th St N (airport land; about 40 acres; project value 32.3M)
program: Tulsa International Airport Development Trust (TIADT) tax increment financing incentives under a development and financing assistance agreement; land lease from Tulsa Airports Improvement Trust (40 years plus two 10-year options)
issuer: TIADT (amount as reported by Tulsa World, which cites the development and financing assistance agreement)
notes: Tulsa World (Rhett Morgan, 2021-05-07, Newmark PDF reprint retrieved from the Wayback Machine because the live PDF returns 403): TIADT 'will provide up to $5.8 million in financing incentives through its Tax Increment Financing District, according to the development and financing assistance agreement'; project worth $32.3M at completion (17.3M real, 15M personal property); at least 200 jobs. The City of Tulsa press release 2021-05-06 (primary, saved) confirms that TAIT leases the land and TIADT provides financing incentives through TIF but states no amount; the agreement text itself was not found. TIF reimburses from the project's own property-tax increment, so it is a cap on reimbursement, not a cash grant. Other coverage (KTUL, KJRH, Public Radio Tulsa, Oklahoma Eagle) repeats the TIF without an amount. Site match: facilities.csv TUL5 is 3400 N Mingo Rd (OSHA); the project is on N Mingo Rd at 36th St N, so probable. A 2021 Tulsa World article by the same reporter ('Amazon blazes development trail') was paywalled in the saved copy.
